summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of AML in remission following stem cell transplant and chronic extensive sclerodermic skin GVHD was admitted for shortness of breath and dry cough. Imaging revealed bilateral lower lobe ground-glass opacities concerning for pneumonia, and he was treated with cefepime and azithromycin. Blood and respiratory cultures were negative, and fungal markers were non-diagnostic. His respiratory status improved, oxygen was weaned, and antibiotics were completed. He developed persistent cough, and CT sinuses showed chronic sinusitis with purulent drainage; cultures were negative, and he was managed with nasal irrigation and topical therapies. IL-2 for GVHD was held initially but restarted. He was discharged home with improved symptoms and instructions for ongoing sinus care and medication adjustments.
